review_candidates.title: Data Analyst (Information Management Associate)
review_candidates.description: As SISSIRP advances into full implementation, there is a critical need for structured information management to ensure that field data is systematically collected, cleaned, analyzed, and translated into actionable programme intelligence for project management, donor reporting, and decision-making. The programme currently operates across multiple data streams — physical progress, WASH outputs, quality assessments, procurement milestones, and beneficiary data — that require integration, visualization, and quality control to meet AfDB M&E and reporting standards. Under the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (Engineering) and the overall guidance of the Programme Manager, the Information Management Associate will serve as the dedicated IM focal point for the SISSIRP programme. The incumbent will design, maintain, and continuously improve the programme’s data collection systems, analytical products, and reporting dashboards, enabling senior programme staff and client management to make evidence-based decisions throughout the project lifecycle. Responsibilities and Accountabilities 1. Data Collection Systems – KoBoToolbox Design, build, and maintain KoBoToolbox data collection forms for all programme components, including physical progress monitoring, QA/QC inspections, WASH output tracking, beneficiary data, and field verification exercises; ensure forms are version-controlled, piloted, and deployed consistently across all four project states. Manage the end-to-end data pipeline from field submission through KoBoToolbox to consolidated datasets: monitor submission rates, identify and resolve data gaps, run automated validation checks (range, logic, required fields), and flag anomalies to field engineers for correction. Develop and maintain standardized data collection protocols and field data submission procedures; conduct remote and in-person training sessions for site engineers and state-level staff on KoBoToolbox form usage, data quality standards, and submission workflows. Support integration of KoBoToolbox data exports with downstream analysis and reporting tools (Excel, Power BI), ensuring data formats, coding conventions, and field labels are consistent and transformation-ready. Maintain and document all active KoBoToolbox projects, form versions, user permissions, and data export schedules; ensure data is backed up and stored in line with IOM data governance standards. 2. Data Analysis and Visualization – Excel & Power BI Build and maintain Advanced Excel workbooks for programme data management and analysis, including: - Dynamic pivot tables linked to live data exports. - Data reconciliation across multiple registers. - Structured data validation and dropdown controls to enforce data integrity. - Conditional formatting for status flags, overdue items, and threshold breaches. - Automated summary dashboards using Excel formulas and slicers to generate programme KPIs without manual recalculation. Develop, publish, and maintain Power BI dashboards providing real-time programme intelligence for SISSIRP management and AfDB reporting. Dashboards should cover: - Physical progress by state, sector, and facility type. - Procurement and contract milestone tracking. - WASH output indicators (coverage, functionality, beneficiary reach). - QA/QC pass/fail rates. - Financial disbursement progress against targets. Apply DAX measures and calculated columns in Power BI to derive programme-level KPIs (e.g., % facilities completed, cost per beneficiary, average construction duration) and configure row-level security to control data access by state and role. Design and implement data models in Power BI connecting multiple source tables (progress trackers, procurement registers, beneficiary data, KoBoToolbox exports) via defined relationships, ensuring dashboard figures reconcile with source data. Produce periodic analytical reports and data summaries (weekly, monthly, quarterly) for the Programme Officer, Programme Manager, and donor reporting requirements; translate data outputs into clear narrative findings with supporting charts and maps. Support GIS-based analysis and mapping of SISSIRP facilities using available tools (Excel/Power BI map visuals, QGIS where applicable) to visualize geographic distribution of project activities and outputs. 3. Programme Reporting and M&E Support Serve as the IM focal point for all AfDB progress reporting requirements: compile, quality-check, and format data inputs from field teams into the programme’s standard reporting templates in line with AfDB M&E frameworks and SISSIRP’s Results Framework indicators. Maintain the SISSIRP master data register: a single source of truth for all facility-level progress data, updated on a rolling basis from field inputs, reconciled against procurement and payment records, and shared with the Programme Officer and Programme Manager on a weekly basis. Support the preparation of donor progress reports, quarterly reviews, and AfDB supervision mission briefings by providing accurate, well-visualized data summaries, programme maps, and indicator tables. Maintain the programme’s document management system for IM-related files, including data dictionaries, codebooks, form versions, and dashboard user guides. 4. IM Capacity Support and Quality Assurance Provide ongoing technical support and troubleshooting to field teams on KoBoToolbox, Excel, and Power BI; respond to data queries from site engineers and state-level staff within one working day. Develop and maintain user guides, data dictionaries, and standard operating procedures for all IM tools and systems used under SISSIRP. Conduct periodic data quality reviews across all programme components; produce data quality assessment reports with findings and corrective recommendations for the Programme Officer. Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the Programme Officer (Engineering) or Programme Manager. Required Qualifications and Experience Education & Experience – Minimum Requirements Bachelor’s Degree in Information Management, Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with four years of relevant professional experience; or Completed High School Degree / Certificate with six years of relevant professional experience. Demonstrated hands-on experience with KoBoToolbox (or ODK/Kobo Collect): designing multi-section forms with skip logic, validation constraints, and repeat groups; managing projects and user permissions; exporting and cleaning datasets. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including: - Dynamic pivot tables and pivot charts. - VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, XLOOKUP. - Nested IF / IFS, COUNTIFS, SUMIFS. - Data validation and structured tables. - Power Query for data transformation. - Conditional formatting and dashboard construction. Demonstrated experience building and publishing Power BI reports and dashboards, including data model design, DAX measures, calculated columns, and Power BI Service publishing and access management. Familiarity with infrastructure, WASH, or humanitarian programme data is a strong advantage. Experience with QGIS or other GIS tools for mapping and spatial analysis is an advantage. Skills Expert-level proficiency in KoBoToolbox: form design (XLSForm or online builder), skip logic, validation constraints, repeat groups, multi-language forms, data export, and project management. Advanced Excel: pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH/XLOOKUP, Power Query (M language), nested formulas, data validation, conditional formatting, dynamic dashboards without VBA. Power BI: data modelling (star schema), DAX (CALCULATE, FILTER, RELATED, time-intelligence), report design principles, Power BI Service (workspaces, row-level security, scheduled refresh, sharing). Strong analytical and data quality skills: ability to identify and resolve inconsistencies, outliers, and gaps in field datasets. Clear data communication skills: ability to translate raw datasets into concise visual summaries, charts, and written findings for non-technical audiences. Proficiency in Microsoft SharePoint / OneDrive for IM file management and team data sharing. Working knowledge of Results Frameworks, Indicator Tracking Tables, and logframe-based M&E; familiarity with AfDB reporting standards is a strong advantage. Ability to manage multiple analytical workstreams simultaneously and deliver outputs to tight deadlines. Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy, consistency, and audit-readiness. DELIVERABLES The Information Management Associate shall produce and maintain the following on an ongoing basis: Maintained and operational KoBoToolbox data collection system across all SISSIRP programme components and states, with version-controlled forms, active user management, and documented protocols. Weekly SISSIRP Master Data Register update: facility-level progress, procurement, and WASH output data consolidated, cleaned, and shared with the Programme Officer. Power BI dashboard suite (programme overview, state-level progress, WASH outputs, procurement milestones) — published, refreshed, and shared with programme management on a rolling basis. Monthly data quality assessment report: submission rates, error flags, correction actions, and unresolved gaps. Quarterly IM inputs for AfDB progress reporting: data tables, indicator summaries, maps, and charts formatted to AfDB reporting standards. IM system documentation: data dictionary, KoBoToolbox form register, Power BI user guide, and standard operating procedures — kept current and accessible to the programme team.

review_candidates.title: All Positions: Steel Plant Director / Chief Hospital Officer / Medical Director
review_candidates.description: Company Description Chip Mong Group is a diversified conglomerate with operations across trading, manufacturing, real estate, banking, retail, food and beverage, and leisure industries. Its core business units include Chip Mong Trading, Chip Mong Industries, Chip Mong Land, Khmer Beverages, Chip Mong Feed, Chip Mong Retail, Chip Mong Bank, and Grand Royal Golf and Resort. The Group also operates strategic joint ventures such as Crown Khmer Beverage Cans, Chip Mong Insee Cement (CMIC) Corporation, and Chip Mong Ritta. With this broad portfolio, Chip Mong Group offers dynamic leadership opportunities and exposure to multiple sectors within a growing regional organization. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site leadership role based in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, encompassing positions such as Steel Plant Director, Chief Hospital Officer, and Medical Director. The role is responsible for providing strategic direction, overseeing daily operations, and ensuring safe, efficient, and compliant performance within the assigned facility or division. Key tasks include setting operational and production targets, monitoring performance metrics, and implementing continuous improvement initiatives to enhance quality, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. The position collaborates with cross-functional teams, manages budgets and resources, and ensures adherence to regulatory standards and company policies. The leader will also mentor and develop management teams, foster a culture of accountability and safety, and represent the organization in internal and external stakeholder engagements. Qualifications Demonstrated expertise in Plant Management and Production Management, with a track record of leading complex facilities or service operations. Strong ability in Production Planning and Operations Management, including resource allocation, process optimization, and performance monitoring. Proficiency in Quality Management, focusing on standards compliance, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement. Extensive leadership experience in industrial, healthcare, or related sectors, managing multidisciplinary teams and large-scale operations. Sound business acumen, including budgeting, cost control, and strategic planning. Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Healthcare Management, or a related field; professional certifications in operations or quality are an advantage. Experience working in emerging markets or regional organizations is beneficial, with the ability to operate effectively in a multicultural environment.

review_candidates.title: After-Sales Service Engineer
review_candidates.description: After-Sales Service Engineer – Wafer AOI Equipment Location: Remote work, with business trips to Vietnam as needed. Travel: 40% within Vietnam Key Responsibilities 1. Independently install, commission, and perform acceptance testing for CFW-series wafer AOI equipment at customer sites. 2. Diagnose and resolve mechanical, electrical, optical, and software issues remotely and on-site. Identify root causes and work with the Zhuhai engineering team on complex issues. 3. Perform preventive maintenance and manage local spare parts and consumables to help maintain equipment uptime of at least 95%. 4. Train customers on equipment operation, routine maintenance, recipe setup, and inspection parameter adjustments. Keep user guides, SOPs, and FAQs up to date. 5. Serve as the local technical contact for customers. Recommend inspection improvements and support equipment demos, sample testing, and defect mapping as needed. 6. Prepare installation, test, and service reports, maintain equipment and fault records, and follow customer site safety and confidentiality requirements. Qualifications - Bachelor’s degree or higher in Electrical, Mechanical, or Electronics Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation, or a related field. - At least 1 year of experience** in field service, installation, commissioning, or maintenance of precision, semiconductor, or electronics manufacturing equipment. - Hands-on troubleshooting skills and the ability to read mechanical drawings and electrical schematics. Experience with AOI, optical inspection, front-end semiconductor equipment, or work in a wafer fab or OSAT facility is preferred. - Familiarity with PLCs, servo and motion control, or machine vision is a plus. - Fluent Vietnamese and sufficient English for technical discussions and documentation. TOEIC 600 or equivalent and Mandarin skills are a plus. - Strong customer service and communication skills, with the ability to prioritize and work independently at customer sites. - Valid Vietnamese driver’s license and willingness to drive to customer sites, travel as required, and attend 1–3 months of technical training in China, after joining.
